extracted.intended_audience: comedy fans, aspiring stand-up comedians, and readers of comedy criticism/tributes
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and qualities that, according to the author, made Greg Giraldo an exceptional stand-up comic — useful for evaluating stand-up performance and craft. Emphasizes originality, delivery tone, stage presence, work ethic, and impact beyond mainstream fame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of material / avoids fabricated stories
rubrics_metrics.description: There are a lot of hack comics that either make up crazy stories about their own life or tell stories they have heard from others and pass them off as their own. Greg never needed to do that, because there was plenty of material on almost all subjects that he had encountered during his life’s journey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authenticity is valued: drawing on real-life experience rather than inventing or appropriating stories marks stronger craftsmanship and credibility onstage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freshness of punchlines on overused topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Anybody can have takes on all of the industry standard topics such as gay marriage, gun control, and terrorism, but not everybody can take a topic that has been run into the ground and come up with a punch line that was the last thing you saw coming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A high-performing comic can reinvigorate clichéd or well-worn subjects by delivering an unexpected or original punchline; novelty on familiar material is a key quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing heavy topics with humility and self-deprecation
rubrics_metrics.description: What was fascinating ... was that he spoke of such large-scale political and social issues without really taking himself too seriously ... he could follow up such heavy topics with a flippant comment such as 'I mean, I think… I could be wrong… Shit, what the hell do I know anyway?' before smoothly transitioning into a bit about some of his personal struggles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid a dogmatic 'I'm right, you're wrong' tone. Using uncertainty, self-deprecation, or a suggestive stance softens heavy material and makes it more accessible and funny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage presence: suggestion over brute command
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though he had a fantastic stage presence, it wasn’t so much about command as it was suggestion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong stage presence does not require domineering control; subtlety and the ability to suggest ideas or perspectives can be more effective than overt command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy, consistency, and reinvention across shows
rubrics_metrics.description: Greg put every last bit of energy he had left for the day into his seven thirty shows and then would somehow miraculously get it all back for the late show and deliver all over again. All the while he was constantly thinking of how to make each show unique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliability (delivering night after night) combined with continual effort to make each set distinct is a valued professional trait for touring comedians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insightful social and political commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestions for how to make the world a better place by pointing out the ridiculousness that lies in every crevice of society’s many ills, suggestions for how to rationalize combative individuals whose stubbornness prevents them from seeing points of view that differ from their own, and suggestions for how to ultimately make himself a better person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy that offers meaningful observations about society and human behavior — not just cheap shots — is praised for depth and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal voice that connects with strangers
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting to the point where you can inject different yet personal takes into the material, and still be hilarious to a room full of strangers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ability to blend distinctive personal perspective with broad relatability — making intimate material land with diverse audiences — is a hallmark of strong stand-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community contribution and legacy beyond mainstream success
rubrics_metrics.description: Just because Giraldo never had a wildly successful television show or didn’t become a huge movie star, doesn’t mean that his contributions to the entertainment community should be anywhere near as understated as they have posthumously seemed to become.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate a comedian's impact not solely by TV/movie stardom but by influence on peers, club work, and contributions to the live-comedy ecosystem.
